correctness.rationale: The prism squares have four signed ±1 color increments summing to zero as an integer (any multiple of five has absolute value <=4), hence top and bottom rim windings coincide. The integer rim sum yields exactly w≡n mod 2 and |5w|<=n, all realizable using one rim sequence and constant vertical sign. Recoloring changes signed increments by an exact vertex coboundary, preserving winding. If |5w|<n, a directed cycle of length L would have integer signed circulation L=5wm with L≥n|m|, impossible for m=0 or |5w|<n. Two colorings of the same winding differ by an exact signed 1-cochain; admissible integer heights form a distributive lattice, and a finite acyclic source-raising argument joins them. A published cycle-target Hom theorem identifies each such acyclic-orientation component with S¹. Extreme winding forces all rim and vertical signs and hence exactly 10 isolated colorings per sign, totaling 20 when 5|n. Independent backtracking enumeration and recoloring-union-find for n=3..8 yielded respective graph-homomorphism totals 0,190,20,1410,560,11070 and exactly the predicted winding components (a check, not proof of the all-n circle type).
residual_risks: Unindexed prism-specialized Hom classification may exist; the S¹ statement relies on Fujii et al Theorem 5.1 and its stated graph assumptions; finite Euler characteristic alone does not identify circle homotopy.
